top_story.headline: Sen. Tim Scott amends 2025 annual disclosure, reporting $94,563 in book royalties
top_story.dek: The amendment was posted 10/06/2026; the filing does not say what changed.
paragraphs: Sen. Tim Scott filed Amendment 1 to his Annual Report for calendar year 2025. It lists $94,563 in royalties from HarperCollins Publishing LLC, retirement income from the South Carolina Retirement System, and spousal wages from MEB LLC of Charleston, South Carolina.

His spouse holds Amazon.com Inc. stock valued at $250,001–$500,000 and several $100,001–$250,000 funds, and the report lists five mortgages, the largest a $500,001–$1,000,000 loan to his spouse from Movement Mortgage (spelled "Movement Morgage" in the filing). The filing text does not identify which items were amended.

sections.headline: No New Divestitures or Terminations Reported
paragraphs: The Office of Government Ethics processed 25 filings during the past three days, with no new divestiture certifications, conflict-of-interest waivers, or termination notices flagged for public attention.

sections.headline: No new or terminated FARA registrants
paragraphs: The FARA e-file reports for 10/05/2026–10/06/2026 each show 0 new registrants and 0 terminated registrants. Sources: New Registrants and Terminated Registrants.

sections.headline: Two House stock-trade reports, two candidate filings and two Senate disclosures
paragraphs: Four House filings and two Senate filings were new in the lookback window; all six were read or are described below, so the 30-filing read cap was not reached. The two House periodic transaction reports are small: one is automatic dividend reinvestment in four stocks, the other a single Treasury bill purchase.

items: Rep. Lloyd Doggett (D-TX37) filed a periodic transaction report on 10/05/2026 listing four purchases of $1,001–$15,000 each, all described in the filing as automatic reinvestment of dividends:

Rep. Vince Fong (R-CA20) filed a periodic transaction report on 10/05/2026 listing one purchase of a U.S. Treasury Bill (0.0%, maturing 12/10/2026), $15,001–$50,000, bought 09/18/2026 and held in a 529 College Savings Plan account. It is a government security, not a tradeable equity, so no trade table is given.

Sen. Tim Scott (R-SC) filed Amendment 1 to his Annual Report for calendar year 2025 on 10/06/2026. Filing. It reports $94,563 in royalties from HarperCollins Publishing LLC, a spouse stake in Amazon.com Inc. stock valued at $250,001–$500,000, and five mortgages, the largest a $500,001–$1,000,000 loan held by his spouse. The filing itself does not say what the amendment changed.

Troy D. Jackson (candidate, Maine) filed a Senate Candidate Report on 10/05/2026. Filing. It lists 2025–2026 self-employment income from International Association of Machinists ($90,000, paid personally and through Jackson Associates, which he solely owns) and International Union of Painters and Allied Trades ($48,000), plus $4,800 from Food and Medicine and $5,100 from Eastern Maine Labor Council. Assets are modest: a Maine public pension and bank, insurance and land holdings.

sections.headline: 36 new lobbying registrations, led by Venezuela energy and defense-bill work
paragraphs: The Senate lobbying database shows 36 new registrations and 542 filings in total posted since 10/05/2026; most of the total are third-quarter activity reports. Three Ballard Partners registrations stand out, two for oil and gas companies seeking Venezuelan opportunities, and Covenant Government Affairs, LLC registered Resource Rock Exploration LLC to arrange an introduction to Venezuela's mining office. Other registrations are routine. Akin Gump Strauss Hauer & Feld registered Proofpoint, Inc. on artificial intelligence and cybersecurity policy, which is also flagged in Industries to Watch.
